div.head: Af 36.1[a]
div.ab: Gif beforan eagum asnæse, gilde þone wer.
Gif beforan eagum asnase, gielde þone wer;
Si ante oculos asnaset, reddat weram eius.
Gif beforan eagum asnase, gielde þone wer.
If he should impale himself before the eyes [of the spear-carrier], let him pay the wer.
If a man is transfixed before his eyes, he shall pay the wergeld;

If he is transfixed before his eyes, he is to pay the wergild; if anyone accuses him of intention in this act, he is to clear himself in proportion to the fine, and by that [oath] do away with the fine,
Wenn er vor den Augen spiesst, zahle er das Wergeld.
If he spits [him] before the eyes, let him pay the wergeld.
div.note: Whitelock translates Af 36.1 as one clause, which the sheet divides into rows 36.1[a], 36.1[b]; her translation of the whole is given here, in the first row.
